before.beta: The easiest way up Ives Peak is a scramble. The standard approach follows the Pacific Crest Trail / Goat Rocks crest, which runs close to the peak's western slopes, then leaves the crest at the col northwest of the peak and follows the northwest ridge and a short south-face scramble to the summit; this is unroped class 2-3 talus/scree, not a technical rock or ice route. A 2026 ski-mountaineering trip report (climberkyle.com) that circled the peak describes the ridge north of the summit as rocky and wind-scoured, with a short loose ('choss') section near the col, and notes lingering snow on the peak's flanks into early summer.
